There is no better way to discover Oakhyrst Grange than by experiencing our school in person.
Our Open Events give prospective families the opportunity to explore our beautiful school, meet our dedicated staff and pupils, and see first-hand what makes Oakhyrst such a special place to learn and grow. As a proud member of the Caterham Family of Schools, we combine over 75 years of educational excellence with exciting new opportunities for our pupils, all while maintaining the warm, family atmosphere that has always defined Oakhyrst.
What to Expect
Whether you attend one of our Open Mornings or arrange a personal visit, you’ll have the opportunity to:
Our Open Events are relaxed, informative and designed to give you a genuine insight into daily life at Oakhyrst Grange.
Tour our beautiful five-acre campus and facilities.
Visit classrooms and see lessons in action.
Open Mornings
Our Open Mornings are held throughout the academic year and provide an excellent opportunity to experience the school during a normal working day.
During your visit, you’ll hear from our Headteacher, tour the school with our pupils and have plenty of time to ask questions and meet members of our teaching and admissions teams.

At Oakhyrst Grange, every child is known, heard and valued.
Our commitment to academic excellence is matched by exceptional pastoral care, ensuring every pupil develops the confidence, curiosity and resilience to achieve their personal best. With small class sizes, specialist teaching, outstanding sporting and creative opportunities, and a strong sense of community, children thrive from Pre-Reception through to Year 6 before progressing to a wide range of independent, grammar and maintained senior schools.

At Oakhyrst Grange School, exceptional pastoral care is at the heart of everything we do. We believe that children thrive when they feel safe, happy and valued, which is why creating a nurturing environment where every pupil is known as an individual is one of our highest priorities.
Our commitment to academic excellence is matched by our dedication to understanding each child personally. We take the time to know every pupil’s strengths, interests and aspirations, ensuring they feel heard, supported and encouraged throughout their journey with us.
A Caring Community
As a small school, we are proud of the close relationships that exist between pupils, staff and families. Every member of our team plays an important role in supporting children’s wellbeing, creating a genuine sense of belonging where every child feels confident to be themselves.
Our warm and inclusive community encourages kindness, respect and compassion. Older pupils naturally become role models for younger children, helping to create a family atmosphere where friendships flourish across year groups.
Supporting Every Child
We understand that every child is unique. Our dedicated staff work closely with families to ensure each pupil receives the support, encouragement and challenge they need to reach their full potential.
Whether celebrating achievements, helping children overcome challenges or building confidence in the classroom and beyond, we take a personalised approach that enables every child to flourish academically, socially and emotionally.
Wellbeing Matters
Children’s emotional wellbeing is fundamental to their success. Through our pastoral programme,’ Roots to Shoots to Mighty Oaks’, pupils develop the skills to:
By fostering these qualities from an early age, we equip children with the confidence to embrace challenges and navigate an ever-changing world. Our dedicated Wellbeing room, ‘The Nook,’ provides a wonderful sensory, calm environment for all pupils to use.
Build positive friendships and relationships.
Develop resilience and confidence.
Understand and manage their emotions.
Show kindness, empathy and respect for others.
Make safe and responsible choices.
Become independent, reflective learners.
Working in Partnership with Families
We believe that the strongest outcomes are achieved when school and home work together. Open communication and strong relationships with parents are central to our approach, ensuring families feel informed, supported and involved throughout their child’s education.
Our staff are always available to listen, offer guidance and celebrate each child’s achievements, creating a partnership built on trust, collaboration and shared aspirations.
A Place Where Every Child Belongs
Pastoral care at Oakhyrst Grange extends far beyond supporting children when they need help—it is woven into every aspect of school life. From the moment children join our community, they are welcomed into an environment where they are encouraged to be themselves, take risks in their learning and grow in confidence.
As part of the Caterham Family of Schools, we continue to build on our long-standing tradition of providing outstanding pastoral care, combining the warmth of our close-knit community with the strength, expertise and opportunities that come from being part of a wider family of schools.
At Oakhyrst Grange, every child is known, every voice is valued, and every pupil is encouraged to flourish.

Years 1–2
At Oakhyrst Grange, our Pre-Prep curriculum provides the perfect balance of academic excellence, creativity and exploration. We believe that children learn best when they feel happy, secure and inspired, so every lesson is designed to nurture curiosity, build confidence and foster a genuine love of learning.
With small class sizes and a caring, supportive environment, every child is known as an individual. Our experienced teachers encourage pupils to become independent learners, resilient problem-solvers and kind members of the school community, laying the foundations for success throughout their education.
Core Subjects
English
Reading, writing, speaking and listening are at the heart of our curriculum. Through engaging stories, imaginative writing opportunities and structured phonics and spelling, children develop confidence in communication while discovering the joy of books and language.
Mathematics
Mathematics is taught through practical activities, games and real-life problem-solving. Children develop strong number skills, mathematical reasoning and confidence while learning to explain their thinking and apply their knowledge in different contexts.
Science
Our science lessons encourage children to ask questions, investigate and explore the world around them. Through practical experiments and hands-on activities, pupils develop curiosity and begin to think like young scientists.
Foundation Subjects
Art & Design
Creativity is celebrated through drawing, painting, sculpture, textiles and mixed media. Children are encouraged to experiment with different techniques, express themselves and take pride in their creations.
Computing
Children develop essential digital skills while learning about online safety, coding and creative computing. Technology is used to enhance learning across the curriculum.
Design Technology
Through designing, making and evaluating, pupils develop creativity, practical skills and resilience while working on exciting projects using a variety of materials.
Geography
Pupils explore their local environment and the wider world, developing an understanding of different places, cultures and the natural environment through practical and engaging activities.
History
Children begin to understand the past by exploring significant people, events and changes over time. Learning is brought to life through stories, artefacts, role play and educational visits.
Music
Specialist music lessons inspire a love of music through singing, rhythm, composition and performance. Children develop confidence while exploring a wide range of musical styles and instruments.
Outdoor Learning
Our beautiful grounds provide endless opportunities for outdoor learning. Through Forest School and nature-based activities, children develop curiosity, resilience, teamwork and a love of the natural world.
Physical Education
Regular PE lessons help children develop coordination, balance, teamwork and physical confidence through a variety of games and activities in a fun and supportive environment.
Religious Education
Children explore different faiths, beliefs and celebrations, developing respect, empathy and an appreciation of the diverse world in which they live.
Swimming
Weekly swimming lessons enable children to build water confidence, develop swimming techniques and learn important water safety skills from an early age.
Learning Beyond the Classroom
Life in Pre-Prep is enriched by educational visits, themed learning days, performances, sporting events, creative workshops and a wide range of clubs. These experiences help children make meaningful connections, build confidence and develop new interests while creating lasting memories.
Building Strong Foundations
Our Pre-Prep curriculum is carefully designed to nurture every aspect of a child’s development. By providing a stimulating, supportive and inspiring environment, we help children become confident, curious and compassionate learners who are fully prepared for the exciting journey into Prep School.

Years 3–6
At Oakhyrst Grange, our Prep curriculum is designed to inspire curiosity, challenge every child and nurture a lifelong love of learning. Combining academic excellence with creativity, practical experiences and outstanding pastoral care, we ensure every pupil develops the knowledge, skills and confidence to flourish.
With small class sizes and specialist teaching across many subjects, we tailor learning to meet the needs of every child. We encourage pupils to think independently, ask questions, solve problems and embrace new challenges, preparing them not only for senior school but for life beyond the classroom.
Core Subjects
English
Children develop strong reading, writing, speaking and listening skills through an engaging curriculum that encourages creativity, critical thinking and a love of literature. From persuasive writing and poetry to class novels and public speaking, pupils grow into confident communicators.
Mathematics
Our Mathematics curriculum develops fluency, reasoning and problem-solving skills. Through practical resources, investigations and real-life applications, pupils gain confidence while being appropriately challenged to achieve their full potential.
Science
Science is taught through exciting investigations and hands-on experiments that encourage children to question, predict and discover. Biology, Chemistry and Physics are explored through practical learning, helping pupils develop scientific thinking and curiosity.
Foundation Subjects
Art & Design
Creativity flourishes through drawing, painting, sculpture, textiles and mixed media. Pupils experiment with different techniques while studying the work of influential artists and developing their own artistic style.
Computing
Children develop essential digital skills through coding, programming, online safety and creative computing projects, preparing them for an increasingly digital world.
Design Technology
Design Technology encourages innovation, resilience and practical problem-solving. Pupils design, make and evaluate products using a variety of materials and tools.
Drama
Drama builds confidence, creativity and communication skills through performance, improvisation and storytelling. Pupils regularly perform in productions and class assemblies, developing self-expression and teamwork.
Humanities
History and Geography lessons bring the world to life through enquiry-based learning, projects and educational visits. Pupils explore different cultures, historical events and environmental issues while developing analytical and research skills.
Linguistics
French is taught by specialist teachers, enabling pupils to build confidence in speaking, listening, reading and writing another language from an early age.
Music
Music is an important part of life at Oakhyrst Grange. Specialist teaching develops musical understanding through singing, instrumental work, composition and performance. Many pupils also participate in choirs, ensembles and productions.
Outdoor Learning
Our beautiful grounds provide the perfect setting for outdoor learning. Through Forest School activities, environmental projects and hands-on exploration, children develop resilience, teamwork and a deeper appreciation of nature.
Physical Education & Games
Our varied PE programme promotes physical fitness, teamwork and resilience. Pupils enjoy a wide range of sports, including netball, football, hockey, cricket, athletics, tennis and gymnastics, alongside competitive fixtures and tournaments.
Religious Education
Religious Education encourages pupils to explore different faiths, beliefs and values while developing respect, empathy and an understanding of the diverse world around them.
Swimming
Weekly swimming lessons help pupils develop confidence and competence in the water while promoting lifelong water safety skills.
Learning Beyond the Classroom
Education at Oakhyrst Grange extends far beyond the curriculum. Educational visits, residential trips, performances, competitions, leadership opportunities, charity initiatives and a wide range of clubs enrich every child’s experience and help them discover new passions.
Preparing for the Future
Our Prep curriculum provides the perfect balance of academic challenge, creativity and personal development. By the time our pupils leave Oakhyrst Grange, they are confident, compassionate and well-prepared for the transition to senior school, equipped with the skills, knowledge and character to thrive in an ever-changing world.

Our broad curriculum, exceptional pastoral care and personalised approach mean that pupils leave Oakhyrst as confident, resilient and well-rounded young people, fully prepared for the next stage of their education.

By the time our pupils leave Year 6, they are independent learners, compassionate friends and confident young people, ready to embrace the opportunities and challenges of senior school and beyond.
Whatever path they choose, Oakhyrst Grange pupils leave with the skills, character and self-belief to thrive.

Art
At Oakhyrst Grange, art is a vibrant and valued part of school life. We believe that creativity is an essential skill that enables children to express themselves, develop confidence and view the world with curiosity and imagination.
Our art curriculum encourages pupils to experiment, explore and take creative risks in a supportive environment. Through drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking, textiles and mixed media, children develop both technical skills and artistic confidence while learning to communicate ideas visually.
Pupils are introduced to a wide range of artists, styles and cultures, inspiring them to broaden their understanding of art and discover their own creative voice. They are encouraged to observe closely, think critically and reflect on their work, developing resilience and pride in the creative process.
Art lessons provide opportunities for children to explore their imagination, celebrate individuality and develop problem-solving skills. Whether working independently or collaboratively, pupils learn that creativity can take many forms and that every contribution is valued.
Artwork is proudly displayed throughout the school, creating a stimulating environment that celebrates achievement and showcases the talents of our pupils. Children also have opportunities to contribute to exhibitions, special projects and whole-school events, sharing their creativity with the wider community.
At Oakhyrst Grange, we nurture young artists by fostering a love of creativity, encouraging self-expression and helping every child develop the confidence to explore, create and inspire.
Forest School
Forest School at Oakhyrst Grange provides children with the opportunity to explore, discover, and learn through hands-on experiences in our beautiful on-site woodlands.
From Pre-Reception onwards, pupils enjoy weekly Forest School sessions led by a specialist Forest School teacher, encouraging curiosity, confidence, creativity, and a lifelong connection with the natural world.
Our woodlands provide a unique outdoor classroom where children can investigate nature, develop practical skills, and learn through meaningful experiences. From observing wildlife and exploring seasonal changes to building dens, creating woodland crafts, and discovering the environment around them, pupils are encouraged to ask questions, solve problems, and develop independence.
Forest School helps children grow in confidence and resilience as they learn to take considered risks, work together, and overcome challenges. Practical activities such as den building, nature exploration, campfires, and roasting marshmallows create memorable experiences while developing teamwork, communication skills, and a sense of achievement.
Time spent outdoors complements classroom learning, allowing children to develop creativity, imagination, and a deeper understanding of the world around them. The freedom to explore and learn in our own woodlands nurtures curiosity and encourages pupils to become confident, capable, and resourceful learners.
At Oakhyrst Grange, we believe that outdoor learning is a vital part of a child’s education. Our Forest School experience inspires adventure, builds resilience, and creates lasting memories, helping children develop a genuine appreciation for nature and the confidence to embrace new challenges.
Linguistics
French is an important part of life at Oakhyrst Grange, giving pupils the opportunity to develop language skills, cultural awareness, and confidence in communication from an early age.
From Reception onwards, children enjoy weekly French lessons with a specialist French teacher. Through engaging, interactive sessions, pupils are introduced to the sounds, vocabulary, and structures of the French language in a fun and supportive environment.
Our approach encourages children to develop confidence in listening, speaking, reading, and writing in French. Through songs, games, stories, conversations, and practical activities, pupils build their vocabulary and develop an enjoyment of learning another language while gaining an appreciation of French culture and traditions.
Learning a language from an early age supports children’s communication skills, curiosity, and understanding of the wider world. Pupils are encouraged to take risks, experiment with new vocabulary, and express themselves with increasing confidence.
As children progress through the school, they continue to develop their French skills, building a strong foundation for future language learning and preparing them for the opportunities and challenges of senior school.
At Oakhyrst Grange, we believe that learning a language opens doors to new experiences and perspectives. French helps our pupils become confident, curious global citizens with a genuine enthusiasm for exploring the world beyond their own community.
Music
Music is an integral part of life at Oakhyrst Grange, providing children with opportunities to express themselves creatively, build confidence, and develop a lifelong appreciation of the performing arts.
From the earliest years, pupils are encouraged to explore and enjoy music through singing, listening, performing, and composing. Our music curriculum develops musical understanding and technical skills while fostering creativity, collaboration, and self-expression. Through engaging lessons, children learn about rhythm, melody, harmony, notation, and a wide variety of musical styles and traditions.
We believe that musical literacy is an essential part of every child’s education. Through weekly curriculum lessons, all pupils are taught to read music confidently, developing the knowledge and skills to understand musical notation and apply it in their own performances and compositions. By the time they leave Oakhyrst Grange, children have a strong foundation in music theory and the confidence to continue their musical journey beyond school.
Singing is at the heart of our musical community. Pupils regularly take part in choir rehearsals, assemblies, concerts, productions, and special events throughout the year. These opportunities help children develop confidence, teamwork, stage presence, and a sense of achievement, while sharing their talents with family, friends, and the wider school community.
Many pupils choose to extend their musical experience through individual instrumental and vocal lessons with specialist teachers. Children can learn a wide range of instruments, including piano, violin, cello, guitar, drums, flute, clarinet, trumpet, and singing, allowing them to discover an instrument that inspires and challenges them. Whether learning for enjoyment, preparing for examinations, or developing performance skills, pupils are encouraged to pursue their musical interests and achieve their personal best.
Music at Oakhyrst Grange is about participation as much as performance. We believe every child should have the opportunity to experience the joy of making music, regardless of ability or previous experience. Through performing, creating, and collaborating, pupils develop confidence, discipline, creativity, and resilience—qualities that enrich their education and remain with them throughout their lives.
At Oakhyrst Grange, music inspires, connects, and empowers our children, helping them to find their voice, celebrate their individuality, and share in the joy of making music together.
Swimming
Swimming is an important part of life at Oakhyrst Grange, providing pupils with the opportunity to develop confidence, physical strength and essential life skills in the water.
From Pre-Reception onwards, children enjoy weekly swimming lessons in our on-site pool, allowing them to develop their skills from an early age in a familiar and supportive environment.
Our experienced instructors encourage every pupil to progress at their own pace, whether they are taking their first steps in the water or refining advanced swimming techniques.
Our swimming programme focuses on building strong foundations in water confidence, safety, stroke technique and stamina. Through regular practice and expert guidance, pupils learn to swim with increasing independence while developing perseverance, focus and resilience.
As part of their swimming journey, pupils also have the opportunity to work towards and achieve Swim England Learn to Swim Awards. These nationally recognised badges celebrate each stage of a child’s progress, providing clear goals, recognising individual achievement and motivating pupils as they develop their skills and confidence in the water.
Swimming is a skill for life, and we believe that every child should have the opportunity to become confident and capable in the water. As pupils progress, they are encouraged to challenge themselves, refine their technique and celebrate their achievements.
Alongside regular lessons, pupils have the opportunity to represent Oakhyrst Grange in swimming galas and competitions. Our teams regularly achieve fantastic results, with children demonstrating commitment, teamwork and pride as they compete for their school.
At Oakhyrst Grange, swimming is about far more than learning strokes; it is about nurturing confidence, encouraging ambition and helping children develop a lifelong enjoyment of being active in the water.
Sport
Sport at Oakhyrst Grange
At Oakhyrst Grange, we believe that sport plays a vital role in every child’s development. Through a broad and engaging programme of Physical Education, Games, Swimming and competitive sport, we encourage every child to develop confidence, resilience, teamwork and a lifelong enjoyment of being active. Our aim is for every pupil, from Pre-Reception to Year 6, to experience success in sport, regardless of ability.
We are incredibly proud that in 2026 Oakhyrst Grange was commended in the Independent Schools of the Year Awards for Sporting Achievement. This prestigious national recognition celebrates our commitment to providing outstanding sporting opportunities, expert coaching and an inclusive programme that enables every child to flourish, whether they are discovering a new sport or competing at the highest level.
Physical Education
Physical Education lessons are designed to build fundamental movement skills, improve fitness and promote healthy lifestyles.
Children in Pre-Reception enjoy two PE lessons each week, with a strong focus on developing agility, balance and coordination through fun and engaging activities, including gymnastics, athletics and ball skills. From Reception to Year 2, pupils take part in a weekly double PE lesson, continuing to develop these essential skills while building the foundations for success in Games lessons.
As pupils progress through the Prep School, PE lessons continue to develop strength, coordination, flexibility and physical literacy, encouraging children to challenge themselves and enjoy an active lifestyle.
Games
Games lessons provide children with the opportunity to develop sport-specific skills, teamwork and a love of healthy competition.
In Reception, Year 1 and Year 2, pupils are introduced to a range of sports through enjoyable activities that develop fundamental techniques, communication and collaboration. From Years 3 to 6, children build their knowledge and skills across football, netball, tag rugby, hockey and cricket. Lessons focus on technical development, tactical awareness and decision-making, preparing pupils to represent the school in an exciting programme of fixtures throughout the year.
Competitive Sport
Sporting competition is an important part of school life, helping children develop resilience, sportsmanship and confidence while proudly representing their school.
Pupils in Years 3 to 6 enjoy an extensive programme of local fixtures throughout the academic year, while Oakhyrst also hosts competitions such as cross-country and hockey using our excellent facilities. Our teams regularly compete in ISA regional competitions across football, netball, swimming, cross-country, athletics and hockey, with many pupils progressing to national finals each year.
Children in Pre-Prep are also introduced to competitive sport through friendly festivals and fixtures with local schools, as well as events involving parents, helping to nurture teamwork, confidence and a love of competition from an early age.
Sport for Every Child
Whether a child is taking their first steps in sport or striving to compete at national level, every pupil is encouraged to participate, challenge themselves and celebrate their achievements. Our inclusive approach, expert coaching and outstanding facilities ensure that every child develops not only sporting ability but also the resilience, determination and teamwork that will benefit them throughout their lives.
Being recognised in the 2026 Independent Schools of the Year Awards for Sporting Achievement reflects our belief that sport should inspire every child to achieve their personal best and enjoy being active for life.
